artists.biography: Swervedriver are an English alternative rock band formed in Oxford in 1989 around core members Adam Franklin and Jimmy Hartridge amidst the shoegazing movement. During their initial decade-long run, the band released four studio albums and numerous EPs and singles despite a considerable flux of members, managers, and record labels. By 1993 the band’s lineup had settled with Franklin on vocals/guitar, Hartridge on guitar, Jez Hindmarsh on drums, and Steve George on bass. A heavier rock sound had also emerged and over the next five years evolved to include elements of psychedelia, classic pop, and indie rock. After losing their fourth label in as many years, the band dissolved at the end of 1998. A continually devoted fanbase of “Swervies” garnered the release of an anthology in 2005 and remastered versions of their first three albums in 2008. Swervedriver reunited for major tours in 2008 and 2012 and are scheduled for an Australian mini-tour in September and October 2013.

perplexity.description:
Mezcal Head, released in 1993, is the second studio album by English alternative rock band Swervedriver. It showcases a distinctive blend of melodic space pop and noisy, dissonant guitar textures, combining elements of shoegaze and alternative rock into widescreen, atmospheric epics. The album's sound is characterized by churning guitars and a dark, cinematic mood, with lyrical themes touching on mystery and motor-driven chaos, exemplified by tracks like "Duel" and "Last Train to Satansville".

Positioned after their debut Raise (1991), Mezcal Head represents a creative peak for Swervedriver, solidifying their cult status within the early 90s alternative scene. Despite internal lineup changes and label difficulties during its production, the album received critical acclaim for its cohesive sound and ambitious songwriting. While it did not achieve major commercial success, Mezcal Head remains a highly regarded work, often cited as a lost classic and a defining moment in the band's discography.
